overview: NEMA 17 is a mounting-face standard (1.7 inch square), not a specific motor — but it's become shorthand for 'the stepper motor 3D printers and CNC machines use.' Unlike the beginner-friendly 28BYJ-48, this is a bipolar stepper: it needs a real stepper driver chip (A4988, DRV8825, or similar) rather than a simple transistor array, and it delivers genuinely useful torque and speed. Standard steppers move 1.8 degrees per step (200 steps per revolution), and — critically — they have no idea where they physically are; all positioning is relative, tracked purely in software from a known starting point (homing).
simpleSummary: A stronger stepper motor used in 3D printers, that needs a real driver chip to run.

specifications.operatingVoltage: Typically driven at 12-24V through a driver (motor's own rated voltage is usually lower)
specifications.holdingTorque: ~26-59 N·cm typical for standard NEMA17 motors

pinMap.name: Coil A+
pinMap.function: One end of motor coil A.
pinMap.gotcha: Never connect/disconnect stepper wiring while the driver is powered — the resulting voltage spike can destroy the driver chip.

pinMap.name: Coil A-
pinMap.function: Other end of motor coil A.

pinMap.name: Coil B+
pinMap.function: One end of motor coil B.
pinMap.gotcha: Swapping a coil's two wires reverses that coil's effective direction — if the motor moves the wrong way, swap one coil's pair (not both).

pinMap.name: Coil B-
pinMap.function: Other end of motor coil B.

useCases.title: 3D printer axis drive
useCases.scenario: The standard motor for X/Y/Z motion and extruder drive in FDM 3D printers.

useCases.title: CNC router/mill axis drive
useCases.scenario: Precise, repeatable positioning for subtractive manufacturing machines.

useCases.title: Camera slider / robotic arm joint
useCases.scenario: Where real holding torque and precise open-loop positioning are both needed.

oftenUpgradedTo: Closed-loop steppers (adds an encoder to detect missed steps) for higher-reliability CNC work
